newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat futures lower on sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat futures lower on sterling strength.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures ended lower after sterling rose against continental currencies today, traders said.
Wheat futures ended down by up to 1 stg per tonne.

There were no fundamental grains markets factors involved, traders said. "There must be more to the grains markets than currencies," one said. But there was not today. "It's getting a bit boring," he said.

The biggest fall was for Mar, which came down by 1 stg per tonne to 95.70 stg on volume of 71 lots. But by far the most traded month was May, which last traded down 0.95 stg at 97.30 stg on volume of 227 lots. Total volume in wheat was 332 lots.

There was no fundamental reason why May should be the most active month for wheat, traders said. But they suggested that it was perceived as the most liquid. Jan or Mar are too close and Jly too far away.

Barley trading was even quieter, with just 32 lots traded. Active month was May, with 22 lots traded. It last traded unchanged at 93.25 stg per tonne. The only move at the end of the day was for Nov, which last traded down 0.50 stg at 94.75 stg on volume of 5 lots.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were again neglected.
